mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in unemployment rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points indicates labor market deterioration, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite UNRATE rising >0.3pp, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales signal weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production signals manufacturing slowdown, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances during late-cycle expansion when INDPRO declines, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in CPI exceeding 0.2% month-over-month indicates accelerating inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as central banks tighten policy.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite CPI rising >0.2% MoM, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in quarterly GDP and industrial production signal a broad-based economic slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when both GDPC1 and INDPRO decline, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payroll employment signals strong labor market conditions, which typically supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS increases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, an elevated federal funds rate above 3.5% is associated with reduced liquidity and higher discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances during monetary tightening cycles when FEDFUNDS > 3.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.
